text: Given an input image, an object detector generates candidate bounding box proposals and extracts their initial region features.
Simultaneously, the input text expression describes the target visual scene along with specific entity relationships.
A language parser converts the expression into a structured scene graph, representing entity phrases as nodes and relations as edges.
In the message propagation module, initial local correspondence beliefs are computed between each entity phrase and all candidate visual objects.
Two parallel passes perform bottom-up and top-down message propagation, using context-sensitive belief selecting and gating to aggregate neighboring evidence.
The updated beliefs pass through an MLP to compute match probabilities, which are minimum-pooled across nodes for image-text matching prediction.
Finally, computing confidence differences across graph edges detects relationship inconsistencies, producing the mismatched relation reasoning prediction.
